after.PASSED and VALIDATED: proposed to the owner as a paper strategy of its own (rule 14), on a 10-year Treasury CFD if the broker quotes one, about twelve events a year, sized by the risk engine, followed forward on paper; never real money
after.otherwise: reported as it is; nothing changes

spec.data: Yahoo daily closes: IEF adjusted for distributions and splits, ^IRX as published (negative and zero yields kept); each file's sha256 in the manifest
spec.events: every auction of a 10-year nominal note (new issue or reopening; not TIPS, not floating), from the Treasury's auction records (fiscaldata auctions_query: dates, terms and type flags only)

gates.both_legs: the short leg's mean net > 0 and the long leg's mean net > 0
gates.costs_x2: mean net per event > 0 with the cost per side and the markup doubled
gates.t: t of the mean net return per event, 2009..2020, >= the threshold
gates.top_year: no calendar year supplies more than 50% of the total

spec.holdout_rule: 2021-01..2026-09: mean net per event > 0 with one-sided t >= 1.645, and > 0 with the costs doubled
spec.question: does shorting the 7-10 year Treasury ETF in the five trading days before each 10-year note auction and holding it long in the five after earn a positive net return at a CFD's costs?
spec.rule: short from the close of trading day a-6 to the close of a-1; flat on the auction day a; long from the close of a to the close of a+5; an auction off IEF's calendar, an event overlapping the previous traded one, or one with unknown financing is no trade
